purpose: Test the apparent contradiction between the lost phallus tradition and posthumous conception of Horus, and audit who actually supplies the river claim before promoting any named actor to misinformation suspect.

source_anchors.claim: UCL summarizes scattered Egyptian references as Isis collecting Osiris's limbs and reviving the body enough to conceive Horus.
The Met summarizes Isis as reviving Osiris after Seth killed him and becoming pregnant with Horus.

Plutarch says Isis did not find the male member, reports it as tossed into the river and eaten by fish, and says Isis made and consecrated a replica. The passage does not name an eyewitness who saw the throw.
Plutarch later says Osiris consorted with Isis after his death and she became mother of Harpocrates.
Diodorus reports that Typhon threw the privates into the Nile because his partners would not receive them; Isis made a likeness and established cultic veneration.
Plutarch preserves a variant in which Isis deliberately distributed effigies / multiple supposed burials so Typhon would be unable to identify the true tomb.

Spieser treats the lost/replaced phallus and post-mortem conception as part of a funerary-religious logic in which preserved or reconstructed genital function symbolizes regeneration and victory over death.

river_claim_audit.implication: Do not treat RIVER as a hard physical endpoint. It is one later literary branch until an earlier Egyptian source independently binds the same custody chain.

conception_paradox.strong_inference: The mythic system preserves generative function after material loss, so the physical original is not demonstrably a single point of failure for conception/restoration.

candidate_explanations.note: Different Egyptian and Greco-Roman traditions need not form one mechanically consistent chronology.
Interesting search branch but not established by the current corpus.

isis_information_control_profile.basis: Plutarch/Diodorus preserve Isis deliberately creating multiple effigies/burial claims to conceal the true tomb from Typhon/Seth.
isis_information_control_profile.reason: She is one of the few actors for whom deliberate control of relic-location information is actually source-bound, but the documented target of that deception is Seth/Typhon, not Sobek.

claim_ceiling: This pass does not accuse Isis of deceiving Sobek and does not prove the original phallus survived. It shows that the river story lacks a named eyewitness in the bound sources, while Isis's protective use of decoys is source-bound and therefore deserves investigation as an information-control node.
